title: Conjecture 1.3
statement_text: The $\mathcal{H}$-square-root problem is NP-complete for the class $\mathcal{H}$ of planar graphs.
context_text: The square $H^2$ of a graph $H$ has the same vertices, two vertices being adjacent iff their distance in $H$ is at most $2$; a square root of $G$ is a graph $H$ with $H^2=G$ (a graph can have several, e.g. $K_5$ has $C_5$ and $K_{1,4}$). For a graph class $\mathcal{H}$, the $\mathcal{H}$-square-root problem asks, given $G$, whether $G$ has a square root belonging to $\mathcal{H}$. It is polynomial for bipartite, outerplanar and proper interval graphs, graphs of girth at least $6$, and trees, cacti and block graphs, and NP-complete for all graphs (Motwani and Sudan), graphs of girth at least $5$, chordal graphs and split graphs. Since these hard classes are relatively dense, it was asked whether the problem becomes polynomial for sparse classes. The authors answer no: the problem (and even its promise version) is NP-complete for the class of $6$-apex graphs, i.e. graphs that become planar after deleting at most $6$ vertices, a minor-closed class at the bottom of the bounded-expansion hierarchy of sparse classes. They ask whether the apex vertices are necessary and believe that already the planar case is hard.
paper_title: Square roots of nearly planar graphs
